_comment: Model registry for the design-iteration harness.
Contract: every model is invoked non-interactively at MAXIMUM reasoning effort,
receives the brief, and PRINTS a complete HTML document to stdout. The runner
extracts the document and writes it to disk. Models never write files themselves —
that keeps the invocation uniform across three different CLIs.
'available' and the invocation flags are VERIFIED on this machine, not assumed.
PRICING is list API price per 1M tokens, used to cost each session. One design =
one session. Prices move — re-check them before quoting these numbers anywhere
that matters. Sources recorded in design/README.md.
'usageBasis' says what the CLI means by the word 'input'. 'inclusive' = its
input_tokens ALREADY CONTAINS the cached tokens (codex). 'exclusive' = the
classes are disjoint (claude, kimi). tools/lib/cost.mjs normalises everything
to disjoint before pricing. Getting this wrong bills cached tokens twice at
the full input rate — which is exactly what r2 and r3 did until 2026-07-26,
inflating GPT-5.6 Sol's r3 session from $1.57 to $7.10.
'priceSource' on each rate block: 'verified' = reconciled against a cost the
vendor itself reported; 'assumed' = list price applied by us, unreconciled.

models.label: Claude Opus 5
models.note: claude 2.1.220. --effort max is the ceiling. --output-format json reports usage AND total_cost_usd, so this model's rates are the only ones in the registry reconciled against a vendor figure. cacheWrite is 10.00 = 2x input, the 1-HOUR cache rate — not 6.25 (=1.25x, the 5-minute rate) as first assumed. Reconciled to the cent on four sessions: r2 opus 1.310906, r2 fable 2.940123, r3 opus 0.7818835, r3 fable 2.789226 all match exactly at 2x and are short at 1.25x.

models.label: Claude Fable 5
models.note: Thinking is always on for Fable 5; depth is controlled by effort. Priced above Opus tier — it has been the most expensive variant in both rounds it ran, on output alone. cacheWrite is 20.00 = 2x input (1-hour cache), same correction as opus5; see that entry for the reconciliation.

models.label: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.note: codex-cli 0.144.3, authed via ~/.codex/auth.json. Flagship tier. TWO THINGS MAKE THIS ONE EASY TO MIS-COST. (1) usageBasis is inclusive: total_token_usage.input_tokens CONTAINS cached_input_tokens — proven from a rollout where turn 1 reads {input 23637, cached 0, output 416, total 24053}, i.e. total == input + output, so cached is a subset. (2) codex exec is an AGENT with repo access and a skills directory, and Sol USES them — unpredictably. r2: 1 turn, 0 tool calls, $0.19. r3: 12 turns, 10 tool calls, 673k cumulative input, $1.57 — it spent its first three turns reading 76KB of ~/.codex/skills/gstack/design-html/SKILL.md, unrelated to this repo, then read the tree, then ran tools/verify-round.mjs against its own draft. Every turn resends the whole conversation, so turn count drives input superlinearly. gpt-terra on the identical prompt made 0 tool calls in both rounds. So a costly Sol session is a BEHAVIOURAL outlier, not a property of the tier — do not generalise from one round. cacheRead 0.50 is the published 10% cached-input discount, ASSUMED not verified — codex reports no cost of its own (this machine is on a Pro subscription, rate_limits.plan_type='pro'), so there is nothing to reconcile against.

models.label: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.note: Mid tier, ~half of Sol. Included specifically to test whether a cheaper tier designs as well against a tightly-specified brief — it has, twice, at a fiftieth of the round's most expensive variant. Same inclusive usageBasis and same assumed 10% cacheRead discount as gpt-sol; see that entry.

models.label: Kimi K3
models.note: kimi -p takes the prompt as its flag VALUE, so -p MUST be last here — the runner appends the prompt after it. --auto is deliberately absent: kimi rejects '--prompt with --auto'. WARNING, corrected 2026-07-26: the previous note here claimed our contract 'needs no tool permissions anyway'. That was wrong. Without --auto kimi still carries its full tool set, and a run asked for a NEW variant instead OVERWROTE design/rounds/r3/variants/kimi-k3-a/index.html — a variant from a finished, committed round. Rounds are supposed to be immutable. tools/lib/repo-guard.mjs now fingerprints the tree around every fan-out and restores anything a model dirtied that it was not asked to touch. Thinking effort is 'high' in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml, its ceiling — there is no per-invocation effort flag, so this one is not literally comparable to the others' max. USAGE: --output-format stream-json prints no token counts, which is why r2 and r3 first recorded cost null. But the CLI does record them — it writes them to its own session log, not to stdout: ~/.kimi-code/sessions/wd_<slug>/session_<uuid>/agents/main/wire.jsonl, as {'type':'usage.record','usage':{inputOther,output,inputCacheRead,inputCacheCreation},'usageScope':'turn'}. Scope is per-turn so these SUM. tools/lib/cost.mjs reads them and matches the session to the run by its created_at. reportsUsage stays false because it reports nothing on the channel we invoke it on. cacheWrite rate is a placeholder — no observed turn has had a non-zero inputCacheCreation. SANDBOXED: kimi is an agent with file-write tools and it once overwrote a variant from a finished round, so generate.mjs spawns it in a scratch dir rather than the repo. Verified 2026-07-26: it still prints the document to stdout and writes nothing. Its usage is read back from the session index, which records the REAL path — matching needs realpath (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp), which is why its cost looked unrecoverable twice.

models.label: OpenCode
models.note: Installed but disabled — it routes across providers, so which model answered would be ambiguous, defeating the comparison. Flip to true and pin a provider to include it.
